issue.title: test_literal_argv_preserves_spaces_and_dashes assumes a bare 'python' on PATH and exits 127 on hosts that only ship python3
issue.description:
`tests/tool/test_executor.py::test_literal_argv_preserves_spaces_and_dashes` assumes a
bare `python` executable exists on `PATH`. It does not on apollo (Ubuntu ships only
`python3`; the workspace interpreter is `.venv/bin/python`), so the child process never
starts and the recipe's exit code is 127:

```
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
>   assert code == 0
E   assert 127 == 0
tests/tool/test_executor.py:82: AssertionError
```

The test body passes `"python"` as the literal argv head:

```python
code = _run("--", "python", "-c",
            "import sys; sys.stdout.write(repr(sys.argv[1:]))",
            "a b", "--", "-n")
```

`which python` -> not found; `which python3` -> `/usr/bin/python3`.

Reproduced 2026-09-20 in workspace sase_10, in isolation and in the full `just
test-scoped` lane, at master `6087c0a8e` and again at `598f1e820`. Deterministic, not a
flake: the interpreter is simply absent, so every run fails identically and immediately
(0.16 s call time).

The test file was added by `1f6adf43b` (`feat(tool): capture ToolRun fingerprints, host
samples, and recording metrics`, 2026-09-19). The fix is to drive the child with
`sys.executable` instead of the bare name `python`, which also makes the assertion about
argv preservation independent of whichever interpreter happens to be first on `PATH`.

Found by the `sase-zr.7` land agent while disposing of the failures phase bead
`sase-zr.7.3` recorded as unrelated to its change ("tools/test_executor literal_argv").
Not caused by epic `sase-zr`, which touches no ToolRun executor code.

task_type_fields.why_not_flake: The test execs the literal name 'python', which does not exist on this host (only /usr/bin/python3), so the child never starts and _run returns 127 on every attempt. Reproduced in isolation and in the full scoped lane at two different master SHAs, identical failure each time.

payload.entry: Fixed by the sase-135 land agent: tests/tool/test_executor.py:75 now passes sys.executable instead of the bare name 'python' as the literal argv head, matching what the smoke harness already does (tools/_smoke_tool_runs_helper.py:62 maps 'python' to sys.executable). This keeps the test's actual subject — that spaces, a bare '--' and a leading-dash argument survive to the child's sys.argv — independent of whichever interpreter happens to be first on PATH. Accepting this as epic sase-135 work rather than an unrelated CI failure: the test was added by epic commit 1f6adf43b (phase 5, sase-135.5), so the portability defect is the epic's own. Verified on athena at master 9a56fc1294: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/tool/test_executor.py -q -> 14 passed in 4.96s. Athena masked this because a pyenv shim provides /home/bryan/.pyenv/shims/python; apollo, where you reproduced it, ships only python3.
